blindSummary:
This state/province holds a dedicated integral law on the right to identity and gender expression (2017) alongside a general LGBT-protection statute (2018), making it one of only three states/provinces to have enacted legislation in both the trans-specific and general-LGBT-equality categories. Unlike one of the other two, which amended and narrowed its provisions in 2023, this state/province's framework is unrevised. The statutory framework supports institutional response channels for a visitor encountering discrimination.

No incident data, enforcement action, or negative visitor-facing finding was located for this state/province in the research pass. Its main city carries a visible and well-established LGBTQ community with dedicated infrastructure. The divergence from the national framework rests on statutory-completeness evidence: an active, unrevised dual-category framework here versus one rolled-back dual-category peer and large peer states/provinces with no such law at all.
blindSourceSummaries: A trans-rights federation's sub-national legislation inventory: lists this state/province's two regional statutes - a 2017 integral law recognising the right to gender identity and expression and a 2018 LGBT persons' equality law - and shows only two other states/provinces holding both a trans-specific and a general LGBT law; the basis for the dual-category claim in the summary.

An LGBT federation's 2025 review of public educational policies across the country's regions: tracks which states/provinces have gender-identity protocols and education legislation; notes this state/province's parliament completing its gender legislation and groups it with four other states/provinces among the leaders on educational-policy coverage.
blindLocalsOnly: The regional identity-and-expression law's registry and administrative procedures operate for residents; a visitor never invokes them.
